column1: # Accesses the installed policy must not grant, at least one per domain. compare_rules.py policy mode fails if any is
# granted in the policy's defaults or with a boolean the module declares at true or at false, except in the one state
# its allowed_when names (<boolean>=true or false). Lines starting with # are comments.

column7: reason
the console measures the key by lstat and never opens it
the console binds tcp 9443 alone, not the rest of Fedora's 9443-9447
the repair console reaches the power helper only
the power helper attests only the repair console
the spool is written once and never emptied by the helper
the excluded-state guard reads subvolume ids, never the product's files
first boot publishes the console's selection, never its key
first boot stats cloud-init's program and never runs it
first boot executes no generic command
first boot reads the public host keys only
executable memory only while olivares_operate_runtime is on
the engine binds tcp 8443 alone, not every http port
the product engine is not an admitted caller of the local API
the product engine does not reach local.sock
repair on tty1 does not depend on the local API
the operations leaf's parent is root's; the portal only searches it
no ancestor of the operations leaf is writable by the portal
the portal places nothing in the lifecycle directory, so it cannot replace the lock
the portal never removes or replaces lifecycle.lock
the portal holds lifecycle.lock read-only and never truncates it
the CLI stats tls.key and never opens it
the CLI never reads the private key
the guard changes profiles only through NetworkManager
netrestore reads the guard's journal only
netprobe writes no NetworkManager keyfile
the product engine never writes the guard's state
the portal never writes the guard's state
the CLI never writes the guard's state
the portal has no writer authority over the network lock
netprobe writes no NetworkManager configuration
netprobe writes no NetworkManager runtime file
the guard adds no keyfile; netrestore alone touches keyfiles
the guard cannot write root's restore ledger
first boot writes no etc_t file; its drop-in has its own type
first boot removes or replaces no etc_t file
